subQuestions.text: The ambient air temperatures during summer and winter in a particular locality are 45°C and 15°C respectively. Find the values of Carnot COP for an air conditioner for cooling and heating, corresponding to refrigeration temperatures of 5°C for summer and a heating temperature of 55°C for winter. Assume suitable temperature differences in the exchanger that exchanges heat with the surroundings. If water from the cooling tower at 30°C is used as a cooling medium with a 3°C temperature differential for air-conditioning in summer, what will be the Carnot COP for cooling? Also, find the theoretical power consumption per ton of refrigeration in each case. Assume no increase in the temperature of the surrounding air or water.

A refrigeration machine using R-12 as refrigerant operates between the pressures 2.5 bar and 9 bar. The compression is isentropic and there is no undercooling in the condenser. The vapour is in a dry saturated condition at the beginning of compression. Estimate the theoretical coefficient of performance. If the actual coefficient of performance is 0.65 of the theoretical value, calculate the net cooling produced per hour. The refrigerant flow is 5 kg per minute. Properties of the refrigerant are:

| Pressure (bar) | Saturation temperature (°C) | Liquid enthalpy (kJ/kg) | Vapour enthalpy (kJ/kg) | Entropy of saturated vapour (kJ/kg K) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 9.0 | 36 | 70.55 | 201.8 | 0.6836 |
| 2.5 | −7 | 29.62 | 184.5 | 0.7001 |

Take $C_p$ for superheated vapour at 9 bar as 0.64 kJ/kg K.
